status: Secondary synthetic experiment; this protocol is recorded before running the new factorial and boundary-support outcomes. It is not an external preregistration.
question: When do regulation inputs reduce load yet consume resources, and how do boundary-target and support interventions interact?
equations: Unchanged model.py; constructed coefficients and existing counter-pathways.
input_subsets: All eight subsets, including the empty and all-input subsets; changes act only during the pulse interval.

boundary_support.meaning: Support marks are raw H before H/(1+H); interventions change only the 5-to-10 network segment. The target changes only during that same segment. All nine conditions share the same preintervention state, coefficients, baseline support, and basal demands.

initialization: Each input-cost coefficient regime has its own stationary state from the same existing upper seed. Within each coefficient regime, every input subset shares that reference. All boundary-support programs share the cost-0.2 stationary state. No coefficients are rebalanced.
context_control: Keep the exact input, target and support intervention program; remove only the elevated opposed demand and retain the aligned basal demand edges.
outcomes: same-cost raw input effects relative to empty subset
same-target support effects relative to raw support 1
interpretation: Model coordinates and times are synthetic; these tests do not establish human efficacy or a calibrated recovery time. Raw program outcomes and the response to an additional demand are distinct estimands. Direct demand and direct support pathways remain active at every boundary target.
